mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 2% YoY and HOUST drops > 10% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) stagnate signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for three consecutive months and GDPC1 flat (<0.2% MoM) over the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals a prolonged contraction in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.
